chunks: It is narrated from Mus'ab ibn Yazid al-Ansari, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام appointed me over four districts of al-Mada'in: al-Bihqubadhat, Bahurasir, Nahr Jawbar, and Nahr al-Malik. He instructed me to levy on each jarib of dense crops one and a half dirhams, on each jarib of medium crops one dirham, on each jarib of light crops two-thirds of a dirham, on each jarib of vineyards ten dirhams, on each jarib of date palms ten dirhams, and on each jarib of gardens that combine palms and trees ten dirhams. He also instructed me to leave every isolated date palm away from the villages for passersby and wayfarers, and not to take anything from it.

And he instructed me to impose upon the dahqins, those who ride thoroughbred mounts and wear gold rings, forty-eight dirhams on each man among them; upon their middle class and their merchants, twenty-four dirhams on each man; and upon their lower class and their poor, twelve dirhams on each person among them. He said: So I collected from it eighteen million dirhams in one year.

key_terms.الدَّهَاقِينِ: landholding notables or local Persian landed elites
key_terms.جَرِيبِ: a measured unit of cultivated land
key_terms.دَرَاهِمَ: dirhams, a monetary unit used for assessment and collection
key_terms.رَسَاتِيقَ: rural districts or administrative agricultural regions

ai.seo_question: What tax rates did Imam 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام assign for land and social classes in al-Mada'in?
ai.summary: This narration reports fiscal directives attributed to Amir al-Mu'minin 'Ali ibn Abi Talib عليه السلام regarding kharaj and graded taxation across agricultural lands and social classes in al-Mada'in. It reflects structured governance, differentiated land assessment, and consideration for public benefit by exempting certain date palms for travelers and wayfarers.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1667 - It is narrated from Mus'ab ibn Yazid al-Ansari, who said:

Amir al-Mu'minin Imam Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) appointed me over four districts of al-Mada'in: Behqubadat, Behrasir, Nahr Jawbar, and Nahr al-Malik. He instructed me to impose the following taxes:
- One and a half dirhams for each jareeb (unit of land) of dense cultivation.
- One dirham for each jareeb of average cultivation.
- Two-thirds of a dirham for each jareeb of light cultivation.
- Ten dirhams for each jareeb of vineyards.
- Ten dirhams for each jareeb of date palm groves.
- Ten dirhams for each jareeb of gardens containing a mix of trees and palms.
He (Imam (as)) further commanded me to leave any stray date palm trees outside the villages for travelers and wayfarers, taking nothing from them.

He (Imam (as)) also instructed me to impose:
- Forty-eight dirhams on the dahqin (landowners) who ride fine horses and wear gold rings.
- Twenty-four dirhams on those of moderate means among them and their merchants.
- Twelve dirhams on their lower classes and poor.
He added: "I collected eighteen million dirhams in one year."
